name: P25G — is the hero's walk TICK running, or has it stopped being called?

steps.note:
RUN IT WITH:  node tools/shoot.mjs --keep-title --url http://localhost:8123/index.html --out /tmp/p25g --script scenarios/P25G-heart.json --timeout 180000

The walk completes its whole route — clean legs, speeds 1.8 to 3.4, never blocked — and then stands at (3.48,-0.76) for 36.5 seconds vibrating at 0.11. The step never finishes. But the guards that would catch exactly that, `H.stall > 0.8`, `leg > 3` and `H.t >= H.timeout`, do not fire, and no error is recorded. A walk that is hung and a walk that is no longer being ticked look identical from the outside.

So: read the walk's own arithmetic DURING the park, not after it. `__DQ.heart()` says how many frames the tick has taken and what it computed on the last one. If `n` climbs while the tail is frozen, the tick is live and the guard is wrong. If `n` is frozen too, nobody is calling it.

steps.eval: (async()=>{await __DQ.storyAuto(false);__DQ.teleport('hollybank',-3.96,-2.12);const r=__DQ.route('at:the chest at the foot of your bed');window.__r=r;__DQ.storyPlay([{op:'move',actor:'hero',to:'at:the chest at the foot of your bed',speed:9}]);return JSON.stringify({issued:__DQ.storyIssued(),mark:r.mark,end:r.end,wp:r.waypoints});})()

steps.msg: the staged walk was ACCEPTED — `storyPlay` returns a promise the runner settles at the END of the beat, so a caller that cannot await it has no way to tell a refusal from a start unless the refusal is reported where it can be read

steps.note: 1. what autoplay(false) ACTUALLY did — it used to flip a flag nothing but the chapter-start hook read, so the chapter simply started the next beat the moment the last one ended and every staged walk below was measuring that beat instead
2. the whole series, and whether `n` ever stopped climbing — a flat counter is a dead tick; a climbing counter with a frozen tail is a guard that is not reaching its test
3. the tail, verbatim, on every sample — this is the walk's own arithmetic and the only thing that says which branch it took
4. and the frames between two adjacent samples: did the counter move at all while he stood still?
5. and the errors, read WHILE it was stuck — the ring keeps the first of every message, so nothing here was evicted
6. did the walk ARRIVE? the mark is the chest's own position, which is jittered between runs, so it is read from the map rather than written down

steps.msg: the staged walk ends UP on the loft, at the chest's own floor — and `steps: 1` above says this was the walk this scenario issued, not a chapter beat it stumbled into
and without stalling: he covered the route, arrived, and the walk ended on its own terms
